Velox Living

We are here so you can be anywhere.

Your property in Transylvania. Managed from anywhere.
Professional property management in Târgu Mureș for remote owners and international investors. We handle everything — tenants, maintenance, bills, and compliance — so you don't have to be there.

--- SERVICES ---

Marketing & Tenant Screening
Professional photography, listings on major Romanian portals, rigorous vetting to find reliable long-term tenants. We verify employment, check references, and assess financial standing before recommending a candidate.

Admin & Legal
Lease contracts drafted in compliance with the Romanian Civil Code. Mandatory ANAF registration completed within 30 days. All documents can be signed digitally — no travel to Romania required. Valid under Romanian electronic signature legislation.

Maintenance & Renovations
We coordinate all repairs, from minor fixes to full renovations, using a network of trusted local contractors. Critical emergencies (burst pipes, heating failures, power outages) receive immediate response. Routine maintenance handled within 24–48 hours.

Bill Payments & Utilities
We pay electricity, gas, water, building association (asociație de proprietari) fees, and taxes on your behalf. Costs are recovered from tenants monthly. Nothing slips through the cracks, and you avoid late-payment penalties.

Rent Collection & Monitoring
Monthly bank transfer collection with payment monitoring. Immediate follow-up on any missed deadlines. Security deposits (typically 1–2 months' rent) managed transparently.

Inspections & Reporting
Move-in, periodic, and move-out inspections with written condition reports and photographs, sent to you digitally. Bi-annual inspections included in our management packages.

Frequently Asked Questions

--- SERVICES & COSTS ---

Q: What does a property manager do in Romania?
A: A property manager handles the full rental lifecycle on your behalf: marketing the property, screening tenants, drafting the lease contract, collecting rent, coordinating maintenance, paying utility bills, ensuring compliance with local laws, and conducting regular inspections with photo reports. For remote owners, we act as your trusted representative on the ground — thousands of kilometres away, you still have full visibility and control over your property.

Q: How much does property management cost in Transylvania?
A: Typically 8–15% of monthly rent, depending on the scope of services included. Full-service packages cover everything from tenant placement to bill payments and maintenance coordination. There are no hidden charges — you agree a clear percentage before we begin any work. Transparent pricing is essential when you cannot oversee the property yourself.

Q: What languages does Velox Living operate in?
A: We operate fully in English, Romanian, Hungarian, and Spanish. This matters practically in bilingual Târgu Mureș — where both Romanian and Hungarian are spoken daily — and for our international clients in Western Europe and Latin America.

Q: How quickly can Velox Living respond to maintenance emergencies?
A: Critical emergencies — burst pipes, heating failures, power outages — receive an immediate response, including outside of business hours. Routine maintenance requests are addressed within 24–48 hours. We maintain a network of trusted local tradespeople who are familiar with our standards and can mobilise quickly.

--- LEGAL & OWNERSHIP ---

Q: Can a foreigner own and rent out property in Romania?
A: Yes. EU citizens have held the same property rights as Romanian nationals since 2007. Non-EU nationals can own apartments and commercial spaces without restriction. Renting that property is entirely legal — you register the contract with ANAF, declare the rental income, and pay Romania's flat income tax. Velox Living handles all of these administrative steps on your behalf.

Q: What are the legal requirements for renting an apartment in Târgu Mureș?
A: You need a written lease contract, ANAF registration within 30 days of signing, and a rental income declaration for tax purposes. The property must also have a valid energy performance certificate (certificat energetic) before it can be advertised or rented. Velox Living prepares all contracts in full compliance with the Romanian Civil Code and manages the ANAF registration process.

Q: Do I need to be present in Romania to sign contracts with tenants?
A: No. Our clients never need to travel to Romania. Under the management agreement, Velox Living is authorised to sign lease contracts with tenants on the owner's behalf. All documents are signed digitally and are fully valid under Romanian electronic signature legislation (Law No. 455/2001).

--- TENANTS & PAYMENTS ---

Q: How do I find reliable tenants in Transylvania?
A: Professional marketing — quality photography, listings on major Romanian portals, clear pricing — attracts the right applicants. We then conduct thorough screening: employment verification, reference checks, and financial standing review. Local market knowledge also matters: understanding which tenant profiles are typical in each neighbourhood helps us match the right tenant to your property.

Q: What happens if a tenant doesn't pay rent in Romania?
A: The landlord issues a formal notice; if unresolved, eviction proceedings can be initiated through the courts. We act well before disputes escalate — proactive communication, clearly drafted lease terms, and security deposit clauses reduce the likelihood of this situation arising. We monitor payments monthly and contact tenants immediately when a deadline is missed.

Q: How are utility bills handled for rental properties in Romania?
A: Utility contracts can be held in the landlord's or the tenant's name, depending on what the lease specifies. For remote owners, Velox Living can hold the utility accounts and pay the bills, recovering costs from the tenant monthly. This keeps accounts organised, avoids penalties, and ensures nothing slips through the cracks.

--- DAY-TO-DAY OPERATIONS ---

Q: What happens during a property inspection?
A: We conduct inspections at move-in, periodically during the tenancy, and at move-out. Each inspection produces a written condition report with photographs, shared with you digitally. This documents the property's condition over time and provides a clear basis for any deposit deductions at the end of the tenancy.

--- GETTING STARTED ---

Q: How do I get started if I live abroad and own property in Târgu Mureș?
A: Schedule a free consultation via the website or WhatsApp. We discuss your property, your goals, and the best management package for your situation. You then receive a management agreement to sign digitally. From that point, Velox Living handles everything: initial inspection, listings, tenant placement, and ongoing management. Many of our clients handed over the keys remotely and have never needed to visit since.

About Velox Living

--- OUR STORY ---

Velox Living grew out of a gap we experienced ourselves. Remote property owners across Western Europe, Latin America, and beyond had no reliable, communicative partner for their Transylvanian investments. The options were either informal arrangements with acquaintances or large, impersonal agencies — neither ideal for someone who cares about their asset but cannot be there in person.

We started as landlords managing our own apartments in Târgu Mureș. We learned firsthand what tenants need, what breaks, what causes disputes, and what matters to an owner at the end of each month. We didn't learn property management from a textbook — we lived it first as landlords.

Today, Velox Living is a family-run team with deep roots in Mureș County. We combine the responsiveness of a personal service with the rigour of a professional management firm. Every property we manage receives the same care we give our own — we have skin in the game.

We work exclusively in Transylvania. That means we know the local market, the contractors, the regulations, and the neighbourhoods with an intimacy that a national agency cannot match. When you work with us, you gain a trusted ground partner — not just a management contract.

Sebastian handles property operations, contractor coordination, and tenant management on the ground. He started as a landlord in Târgu Mureș and understands both sides of the equation — what landlords need and what tenants expect. He knows what tends to go wrong before it does.

We operate fully in four languages: English, Romanian, Hungarian, and Spanish.

This is not a marketing line. It is daily working practice.

In bilingual Târgu Mureș, being able to speak to tenants in Romanian or Hungarian is the difference between resolving a situation and escalating it. For our international clients, receiving reports and correspondence in their own language builds the trust that remote management requires.

What multilingual service means in practice:
- Owner reports are written in your preferred language.
- Tenants are spoken to in their language — Romanian or Hungarian as appropriate.
- Official paperwork (contracts, ANAF filings, compliance documents) is handled correctly in Romanian, as the law requires.
- You need someone who can respond in Romanian AND coordinate a repair — not one or the other.

--- COMPLIANCE & LEGAL REGISTRATIONS ---

ANAF-Registered Operations
All rental contracts are registered with the Romanian National Agency for Fiscal Administration (ANAF) as required by Romanian law. We manage this process as part of our standard service.

Romanian Civil Code Compliance
Lease agreements are drafted in full compliance with the Romanian Civil Code (Codul Civil), protecting both owners and tenants and ensuring enforceability in Romanian courts.

ONRC-Registered Company
Velox Living is a legally registered entity in Romania (Registrul Comerțului — ONRC), providing formal accountability and legal standing as your management partner.

Digital Signing Ready
All contracts can be signed remotely — no travel to Romania required. Fully valid under Romanian electronic signature legislation (Law No. 455/2001).

Pricing

There are no setup fees. No add-on charges for services that should be included. No surprises at the end of the month.

--- OPTIONAL SERVICES & ADD-ON COSTS ---

Some tasks fall outside the scope of routine management. These are charged separately at agreed rates:

Contract renewal / redrafting: 150–250 RON per operation
Applies when an existing lease expires and a new agreement must be drafted for the same or a new tenant.

Major works coordination: 5% of work value (minimum 150 EUR)
For significant refurbishments or renovations. The owner pays directly for materials and labour; Velox Living manages the process, contractors, and quality control.

Professional cleaning coordination (move-in / move-out): 10% of the cleaning company's cost
We source, schedule, and oversee the cleaning company. The cleaning cost itself is charged directly to the owner or deducted from the security deposit as appropriate.

ANAF contract registration: 200 RON
The mandatory ANAF registration required within 30 days of lease signing. Included in our full management packages; charged separately if requested as a standalone service.

ANAF income declaration assistance: from 200 RON per year
Support preparing and filing the annual rental income declaration with ANAF. Recommended for owners who want to ensure compliance without engaging a separate accountant.

Eviction assistance / lease termination: from 500 RON
Legal and procedural support for lease termination or eviction proceedings. Cost varies based on complexity and whether court involvement is required.

--- TENANT GUARANTEE ---

3-Month Tenant Guarantee

If a tenant placed by Velox Living vacates within the first three months — for any reason — we find the next tenant at no additional charge. This applies to both management packages.

We back our screening process with this guarantee because we are confident in our methodology. If the tenant doesn't work out, neither should you bear the cost of finding another.

What Remote Owners Need to Know About Renting Property in Romania in 2026

Published: June 2026 | Read time: 8 minutes
Audience: Remote property owners, diaspora Romanians

--- LEGAL REQUIREMENTS FOR RENTING PROPERTY IN ROMANIA ---

The rental contract (contract de închiriere) must be in writing to be legally enforceable. A verbal agreement carries no weight in court. The contract must include: the full names and ID details of landlord and tenant, a description of the property, the monthly rent, the lease term, security deposit terms, and each party's responsibilities for utilities and maintenance.

Contracts can be signed electronically and are valid under Law No. 455/2001 on electronic signatures — this is the legal basis for remote management.

ANAF Registration

Within 30 days of signing the lease, the contract must be registered with ANAF (the Romanian National Agency for Fiscal Administration). Failure to register exposes the landlord to administrative fines and may make the contract unenforceable in court. Registration can be done online via the ANAF portal (with a qualified digital certificate) or in person at the local tax office.

Energy Performance Certificate

Before a property can be advertised or rented, it must have a valid energy performance certificate (certificat de performanță energetică). This classifies the property on a scale from A (most efficient) to G (least efficient). It is required by law and inspectors may ask to see it.

--- TAX OBLIGATIONS FOR LANDLORDS ---

Romania applies a flat 10% income tax on rental income. There are two calculation methods:

Standard deduction (default): ANAF applies an automatic 40% expense deduction. Tax = 10% of 60% of gross annual rental income. No documentation required.

Actual expenses method: If you spend more than 40% of rental income on documented expenses (repairs, maintenance, insurance, depreciation), you can declare actual expenses instead. Requires bookkeeping and documentation.

Example: A property renting at €400/month generates approximately RON 24,000 in annual income (at current exchange rates). With the standard 40% deduction, taxable income = RON 14,400. Annual tax = RON 1,440 (approximately €290).

Non-resident landlords are still obligated to declare and pay Romanian income tax on Romanian-source rental income. Romania has double taxation treaties with most EU countries, so you typically will not pay twice. Confirm with a tax adviser in your country of residence.

Building association fees (asociație de proprietari) are charged monthly per apartment. These are the landlord's responsibility, though the lease may specify that the tenant reimburses them.

--- HOW RENT COLLECTION WORKS ---

The most reliable method is monthly bank transfer. Cash payments are legally permitted but harder to document for tax purposes.

Security deposits: Market practice in Târgu Mureș is 1–2 months' rent. The deposit is held by the landlord or management company for the duration of the tenancy and returned within a reasonable period after move-out, minus legitimate deductions for unpaid rent or damage beyond normal wear and tear.

Currency: Rents are often quoted in euros to protect against currency fluctuation. If payment is made in RON, the contract should specify the exchange rate mechanism.

Late payments: A well-drafted lease should include penalty clauses for late payment. A property manager monitors payment deadlines monthly and contacts the tenant immediately when a transfer is missed — before the situation becomes a formal dispute.

--- TENANT RIGHTS IN ROMANIA ---

Romanian law provides meaningful tenant protections. Remote owners should understand these:

No eviction without a court order. Even if a tenant breaches the contract, they cannot be removed without going through the courts.

Minimum 30 days' written notice is required to terminate an open-ended contract (some courts have interpreted this period as longer). A fixed-term lease ends on its stated date without notice, unless renewed.

The tenant has the right to use the property undisturbed. The landlord cannot enter the property without the tenant's permission except in a genuine emergency.

Regular inspections must be pre-agreed in the lease. Inspections without prior notice or agreement can constitute a breach.

Rent is frozen during a fixed-term contract. The landlord cannot unilaterally raise rent mid-contract. Increases can only be applied at the start of a new lease term.

These protections make careful tenant selection the single most important risk management tool available to a landlord.

--- HOW TO HANDLE MAINTENANCE FROM ABROAD ---

Romanian law is clear on responsibility: the landlord is responsible for structural repairs and major systems (heating, plumbing, electrical). The tenant is responsible for minor day-to-day upkeep (replacing light bulbs, clearing blockages, general cleaning).

In practice, building a reliable contractor network from abroad is nearly impossible alone. A property management company maintains pre-vetted relationships with local plumbers, electricians, locksmiths, and general tradespeople who understand the standards expected and can mobilise quickly.

True emergencies — burst pipes, heating failures in winter, power outages — cannot wait for a remote owner to research solutions across time zones. Having a local management company with 24/7 emergency response protocols limits damage and keeps tenants safe.

--- WHY PROFESSIONAL PROPERTY MANAGEMENT IS THE SAFEST APPROACH ---

The real costs of self-managing a Romanian property from abroad:
- Navigating Romanian-language bureaucracy: ANAF filings, contract compliance, official correspondence
- Sourcing and vetting contractors remotely without local knowledge
- Handling tenant disputes without on-the-ground presence or local legal knowledge
- Responding to maintenance emergencies across time zones

A single poorly selected tenant or unresolved maintenance issue can cost far more than a year's worth of management fees.

A full-service property manager handles: marketing and photography, tenant screening and references, lease drafting and ANAF registration, monthly rent collection and payment monitoring, utility bill management, maintenance coordination, building association payments, periodic inspections with photo reports, and owner communication in the owner's preferred language.

Management fees are typically 8–15% of monthly rent. On a €400/month apartment, that is €32–60/month — largely offset by lower vacancy rates (professional marketing reduces downtime) and avoided legal and maintenance risks.

Key facts for 2026:
- Rental income tax: 10% flat
- Standard expense deduction: 40%
- ANAF registration deadline: 30 days from lease signing
- Security deposit: typically 1–2 months' rent
- Eviction notice (open-ended contract): minimum 30 days
- Property management fees: 8–15% of monthly rent

Property Management in Târgu Mureș: A Complete Guide for Investors

Published: June 2026 | Read time: 10 minutes
Audience: Investors evaluating the Târgu Mureș market

--- WHY TÂRGU MUREȘ IS AN INTERESTING INVESTMENT MARKET ---

Târgu Mureș is the capital of Mureș County and one of Transylvania's principal cities, with a population of approximately 120,000–130,000. It is genuinely bilingual — Romanian and Hungarian are spoken daily — which expands the tenant pool and reflects the city's cultural depth.

Demand drivers:

Medical and pharmacy students: George Emil Palade University of Medicine, Pharmacy, Science and Technology (UMFST) is one of Romania's leading institutions in its field, with approximately 10,000 students. Many rent privately. Medical programmes run 6 years, meaning students are long-term, reliable tenants.

Healthcare sector: Multiple hospitals and medical research institutions provide stable employment and generate consistent demand from healthcare professionals.

Industrial employment: Major employers including Romgaz (Romania's state gas producer) and international manufacturing companies in the city's industrial zone provide stable working-class rental demand.

Bilingual tenant pool: The city's Romanian-Hungarian character attracts tenants from both linguistic communities, broadening demand relative to a monolingual city of equivalent size.

Infrastructure: Târgu Mureș has an international airport (TGM) with connections to major European hubs, and good road links to Cluj-Napoca (~110 km) and Brașov (~150 km). This makes the city accessible for periodic visits and supports genuine long-term growth potential.

Property prices in 2026: Existing residential stock trades at €800–€1,400/m². New-build developments reach €1,500–€1,900/m². These figures represent a 40–60% discount versus Bucharest and Cluj-Napoca.

The highest rents relative to purchase price are found in the central and western residential areas: Tudor, Unirii, and Cornești.

--- AVERAGE RENTAL YIELDS ---

Gross yields in Târgu Mureș range from 5–8% per year, depending on property type, neighbourhood, condition, and tenant quality.

Example: A 2-bedroom apartment in Tudor renting at €420/month with a purchase price of €80,000 produces a gross yield of 6.3%.

After accounting for management fees (~10%), building association fees, and income tax (10% on 60% of gross income under the standard deduction), net yield lands in the 4.5–5.2% range.

Yields by property type:
- Studio / 1-bedroom: 6–8% (strong student demand, very low vacancy)
- 2-bedroom: 5.5–7% (most liquid segment; couples, young professionals, medical residents)
- 3-bedroom: 5–6.5% (families and shared professionals; slightly longer void periods)
- Commercial / retail: can exceed 8% (higher risk; specialist knowledge required)

--- HOW TRANSYLVANIA DIFFERS FROM BUCHAREST ---

Lease length: Târgu Mureș averages 12–24 months (long-term, stable). Bucharest averages 6–12 months (often shorter, more transactional).

Tenant profile: Târgu Mureș draws students, medical staff, and local workers seeking stable long-term accommodation. Bucharest draws corporate expats, young professionals, and short-stay tenants.

Short-term rental market: Limited and niche in Târgu Mureș. Well-developed in Bucharest.

Price per m²: €800–€1,400 in Târgu Mureș versus €1,800–€3,500+ in Bucharest.

Gross yield potential: 5–8% in Târgu Mureș versus 4–6% in Bucharest.

Price appreciation: Moderate and stable in Târgu Mureș. Higher in Bucharest, but also more volatile.

Management complexity: Lower in Târgu Mureș due to stable, long-term tenancies. Higher in Bucharest due to greater turnover and compliance burden.

The key distinction is that Târgu Mureș is a long-term rental market. The student and professional tenant base tends to stay for one to several years. Lower turnover means lower re-letting costs, more stable cash flow, and simpler management. For investors seeking passive income rather than short-term capital gains, this stability is a significant advantage.

--- WHAT A PROPERTY MANAGER HANDLES VERSUS WHAT THE OWNER DECIDES ---

What Velox Living handles (day-to-day):
- Professional photography and listing creation on major Romanian portals (OLX Imobiliare, Storia, Imobiliare.ro)
- Tenant enquiry management, viewings, and application screening
- Employment verification and reference checks
- Lease contract drafting per the Romanian Civil Code
- ANAF registration within the 30-day window
- Monthly rent collection and payment monitoring
- Immediate follow-up on late or missed payments
- Utility bill payments (electricity, gas, water, internet)
- Building association (asociație de proprietari) fee payments
- Coordination of all maintenance and repairs with pre-vetted contractors
- 24/7 emergency response for urgent issues
- Periodic property inspections with photo reports sent to the owner
- End-of-tenancy inventory checks and deposit reconciliation
- Owner communication in English, Romanian, Hungarian, or Spanish

What the owner decides:
- Major renovation or refurbishment projects (above the agreed spend threshold)
- Rent level and lease terms at each new tenancy
- Final approval on tenant candidates (if the owner wishes to retain this decision)
- Annual tax filings (or delegation to a local accountant)
- Long-term strategic decisions: hold, sell, or refinance

Every step of Velox Living's onboarding and ongoing management can be completed remotely. Management agreements are signed digitally. Lease contracts are signed on the owner's behalf under the management mandate. Monthly reports are sent by email. You can own and manage a property in Târgu Mureș from anywhere in the world.

--- STEP-BY-STEP: HOW TO WORK WITH VELOX LIVING ---

Step 1 — Free Consultation
Contact us via WhatsApp, email, or the consultation form on the website. We discuss your property, your goals, and current market conditions. No obligation. Always free.

Step 2 — Property Assessment
We assess the property — in person if we have access, or remotely via photos and documentation. We give an honest opinion on the realistic rental value, any improvements worth making before listing, and realistic expectations for yield and tenant timeline.

Step 3 — Management Agreement
We prepare a management agreement setting out responsibilities, fee structure, and spend approval thresholds for maintenance decisions. Signed digitally — no travel required. We agree on the target rent and desired tenant profile.

Step 4 — Tenant Search and Screening
Professional photography, listings on major Romanian portals. We manage all enquiries, conduct viewings, screen applicants, verify employment and references, and present a recommendation. The owner always has final approval on the tenant.

Step 5 — Lease Signing and ANAF Registration
We draft the lease in compliance with the Romanian Civil Code, sign on your behalf under the management mandate, and register the contract with ANAF within 30 days. You receive a copy of the signed contract and the ANAF registration confirmation.

Step 6 — Ongoing Management
We handle everything: monthly rent collection, payment monitoring, utility bills, building fees, maintenance requests, and periodic inspections. You receive a monthly report covering rent received, expenses incurred, and relevant updates. All communication in your preferred language.

Step 7 — Annual Review
Once a year, we review performance: yield achieved, rental market evolution, maintenance history, and tenant satisfaction. We advise on whether a rent adjustment is appropriate at the next renewal, and flag any capital maintenance items worth planning ahead.

- Average 2-bedroom rent: €350–€500/month
- Gross yield: 5–8%
- Average lease term: 12–24 months
- Management fee: 8–15% of monthly rent
